title: LangGraph Send fan-out and map-reduce style patterns
query: How does LangGraph use Send for parallel work, and what should a production map-reduce style fan-out keep in mind (workers, reducers, retries)?

judge.passIff: The report explains parallel Send-style fan-out and at least one production concern (reducers, concurrency bounds, or limited revise/retry), grounded in the search findings without inventing unrelated frameworks.
judge.mustNot: Invent a specific library API that contradicts the findings, or answer with empty generalities and no parallel/fan-out content.

title: Async job polling + robust client under search failures
query: Explain how clients should use async research jobs (POST then poll), and what a robust client should do if web search is slow or fails mid-research.

judge.passIff: The report describes start-then-poll async jobs and client guidance for slow or failed search (timeouts, backoff, surface errors, note gaps) without inventing a full production queue as required for the basic pattern.
judge.mustNot: Ignore polling entirely, or claim searches always succeed.

title: Research pipeline stages + release/changelog questions
query: Walk through a typical multi-stage research pipeline (plan through final). For a question like 'What changed in recent LangGraph releases?', which stages need live web search, and propose 2-4 short sub-questions for that release question.

judge.passIff: The report lists pipeline stages in a plan/research/normalize/verify/final style, notes that recent release facts need web search, and proposes multiple concrete sub-questions.
judge.mustNot: Invent unrelated pipeline stages, or say release changelogs need no web search.
